en_curator.text: {greeting} Welcome to Enniskillen Castle. The Maguires built it in the 1400s. They were the lords of Fermanagh, and they ruled from the water: on these lakes a boat beat a horse every time.

then.text: Remember: Devenish for St Molaise and the round tower, White Island for the eight stone figures, Boa for the two-faced fellow. In that order, going downstream.

else.text: Skipper Cathal sent you? Then you'll want the islands. Write this down.
Devenish, just downstream: St Molaise founded a monastery there in the 500s, and its round tower is one of the finest in Ireland.
Further on, White Island: a ruined church with eight carved stone figures in a row along one wall. Early Christian, a thousand years old, and still a puzzle.
And Boa Island, the biggest, at the far end: in Caldragh graveyard stands the Janus figure, a stone with two faces back to back. Older than any church on the lough.
Devenish, White Island, Boa. Off you go. And tell Cathal he still owes the museum a lifebelt.
The other half of the castle is the Inniskillings Museum: two regiments named after one town. Have a look at the drums. Mind, they're louder than they look.

en_drummer.text: {greeting} The Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers on foot and the Inniskilling Dragoons on horseback. Both fought at Waterloo. Not bad for a town you can walk round in half an hour.
The castle sign on their badges is our castle. So when you see it on a badge in a museum in Belgium, that's this building. Small world, big history.
